instruction: Pat the chicken dry and season with black pepper.
detail: Dry skin browns instead of steaming; season both sides.

instruction: Heat the cooking oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
detail: The oil is ready when a drop of water sizzles.

instruction: Brown the chicken on all sides in batches.
detail: Give each piece room; crowding steams the meat.

instruction: Add the garlic and cook until fragrant. Pour in the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and 120 ml water.
detail: Let the vinegar bubble before stirring so it mellows.

instruction: Add the bay leaves, cover, and simmer until the chicken is tender.
detail: Tender means a fork twists easily in the meat.

instruction: Uncover and reduce the sauce, spooning it over the chicken.
detail: It is ready when the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Spoon the sauce over each serving.

instruction: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then drain it well.
detail: Shake the colander dry so the grains toast instead of steam.

instruction: Simmer the rice in a covered pot until tender, then spread it on a tray.
detail: The lid stays on; the steam finishes the rice.
caution: Steam is hot; lift the lid away from you.

instruction: Fry the garlic in hot oil until golden, then add the rice and toss to coat.
detail: Golden, not brown; burnt garlic turns the rice bitter.

instruction: Press the rice into the pan and let it crisp underneath before tossing again.
detail: A dark, toasty crust is the point; listen for the sizzle.

instruction: Season with salt and pepper, scatter the spring onion, and serve.
detail: Taste once more before it leaves the pan.

instruction: Pat the pork belly dry, score the skin, and season both sides with salt and black pepper.
detail: Score through the skin only, about a finger apart.
caution: Keep the knife shallow; score the skin only.

instruction: Bring a pot of water to a boil with the garlic and bay leaves.
detail: Enough water to cover the pork belly.
caution: Hot water; lower the pork in gently.

instruction: Boil the pork belly with the aromatics until the meat is tender, skimming the surface.
detail: A fork should slide into the meat with little resistance.

instruction: Drain the pork belly and dry the skin with paper towels.
detail: Dry skin is what crisps; blot every corner.

instruction: Rub the skin with cooking oil, then air-fry at 200 °C until it puffs and crackles.
detail: Arrange the pieces so the skin has room to bubble.
caution: Hot fat; open the basket away from you.

instruction: Rest the pork belly on a rack, then chop it into pieces. Serve with banana ketchup and a soy-vinegar dip with calamansi and spring onion.
detail: Chopping skin-side up keeps the crackling intact.
